project.title: TMEM160 Promotes Tumor Growth in Lung Adenocarcinoma and Cervical Adenocarcinoma Cell Lines
project.projectDescription: This dataset corresponds to the proteomic characterization of the TMEM160 interactome in A549 cells using co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) followed by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS). TMEM160 was immunoprecipitated using an anti-TMEM160 antibody, and interacting proteins were identified through LC–MS/MS analysis using a Q-Exactive HF-X system. Protein identification and quantification were performed in DIA-NN (v1.8.1) in library-free mode using the UniProt Human reference proteome.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Sample Preparation and Co-IP: A549 cells were cultured to 80–90% confluence and lysed in NP40 lysis buffer containing 0.5% CHAPS and protease/phosphatase inhibitors. Lysates were incubated with protein A/G agarose beads conjugated to anti-TMEM160 antibody, crosslinked with BS3. Negative controls were prepared identically but without the primary antibody. Bound proteins were eluted under acidic conditions, neutralized, and processed for MS-based proteomics. Protein Digestion: Eluted proteins were reduced with DTT, alkylated with iodoacetamide, precipitated with cold ethanol, and digested overnight with trypsin (1:50). Sodium deoxycholate was removed via ethyl acetate extraction. Peptides were desalted using Sep-Pak tC18 cartridges and dried prior to LC–MS/MS analysis. LC–MS/MS Analysis: Peptides were separated using a Dionex Ultimate 3000 RSLCnano UPLC coupled to a Q-Exactive HF-X mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). One microgram of peptides was loaded onto an Acclaim PepMap100 trap column and separated on a 50 cm EASY-Spray C18 analytical column at 300 nL/min. A 60-min nonlinear gradient was applied. Data were acquired using a variable-window DIA method (54 MS2 windows, 385–1460 m/z). MS1 resolution was 120,000 (200 m/z) and MS2 resolution was 30,000.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw DIA files were processed using DIA-NN v1.8.1 in library-free (direct) mode. The UniProt Human reference proteome (2020 release) was used as the FASTA database. DIA-NN parameters included a precursor mass range of 300–1800 m/z, fragment mass range of 200–1800 m/z, trypsin specificity with up to two missed cleavages, fixed carbamidomethylation on cysteines, and variable methionine oxidation. Peptide and protein false discovery rate (FDR) was controlled at 1%. Quantification was performed using peak-center intensities with automatic mass accuracy optimization.  Protein intensity matrices generated by DIA-NN were analyzed in Perseus v2.0.10.0, log2-transformed, and median-normalized. Differential enrichment between TMEM160 Co-IP and negative controls was assessed using Student’s t-tests with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction. Functional enrichment (GO, KEGG, Reactome, GSEA) was performed on normalized protein-level data.
